cultural.vision_reason: Feather cape ('ahu'ula fragment) made of 'i'iwi and mamo feathers on olonā fiber netting — a classic Native Hawaiian chiefly garment.

physical.title: cape
physical.summary:
Cape (possibly a section of an ‘ahu’ula) made of red 'i'iwi and yellow mamo feathers (possibly some yellow ʻōʻō feathers) attached in bundles to an olonā fibre nae (net). The cape is shallowly curved and has a wide, almost straight, neckline and short collars.  
Yellow feathers are arranged into a band of seven niho (triangles) pointing up to the neckline along the top of the cape. Beneath them are two yellow loops and a band of yellow runs along the edge of the cape. The rest of the cape is red. Some of the yellow feathers have been trimmed to give a crisp edge between the yellow and red sections.  
The feathers are attached to the olonā nae in bundles. A plaited olonā fibre cord runs along the neckline and collars; the cords extend beyond the neckline where they taper and end in a knot. On the proper right there is a piece of kapa (barkcloth) tied to the end of the cord. The plaited olonā cords also extend slightly below the collar where they are cut short.  
The edge of the nae is roughly cut in places, with the bottom edge of the nae extending past the feathers in some areas.
